'''Schoettler:''' {{legend0|#a5b0ff|40–50%}} {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} {{legend0|#6674de|60–70%}} | title = Governor | before_election = [[Roy Romer]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Bill Owens (Colorado politician)|Bill Owens]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsCO}} The '''1998 Colorado gubernatorial election''' was held on November 3, 1998 to elect the [[List of governors of Colorado|governor of Colorado]]. Under newly applicable term limits, Democratic incumbent [[Roy Romer]] was unable to seek re-election. In the open race to succeed him, Colorado treasurer Bill Owens defeated lieutenant governor Gail Schoettler. Schoettler won the Democratic primary over Colorado Senate minority leader Mike Feeley. In the Republican primary, Owens defeated Senate president Tom Norton by a relatively wide margin. This was the last election in which Colorado held separate primary elections for governor and lieutenant governor; following a statutory change in 2000, candidates selected running mates prior to the primary.{{cite journal |last=Yeargain|first=T. Quinn|date=2021|title=One Vote, Two Winners: Team-Ticket Gubernatorial Elections and the Need for Further Reform|url=https://repository.law.miami.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=4637&context=umlr|journal=University of Miami Law Review|volume=75|issue=3|pages=779|doi= |access-date=June 14, 2021}} In the general election, Owens narrowly defeated Schoettler, aided by a strong performance by U.S. senator [[Ben Nighthorse Campbell]] in his [[1998 United States Senate election in Colorado|re-election campaign]]. Owens's narrow election meant that he was the first Republican governor in 24 years. His running mate [[Joe Rogers (politician)|Joe Rogers]] became the second [[African Americans|African American]] lieutenant governor in the state's history after [[George L.
